correctness.rationale: The group law gives exactly the pairwise determinant condition and q^(mr) freely chosen central coordinates; the wording at RESULT.md line 31 about free coordinates should be read as c_i alone, as in the proof at line 34. An independent all-parameter count uses the valuation i of the ideal generated by the first matrix row. If that row is zero, the second row is arbitrary. Otherwise a GL_r(R) change of columns sends the first row to (pi^i,0,...,0), which preserves the vanishing-minor condition and makes each of the last r-1 second-row entries lie in Ann(pi^i), of size q^i. Thus D_r=q^(mr)+sum_{i=0}^{m-1}(q^(r(m-i))-q^(r(m-i-1))) q^m q^(i(r-1)). Summing gives q^(mr)+(A_m-1)(q^r-1)q^((m-1)r), exactly the claimed expression after the central factor. The frozen proof's common-valuation count reaches the same sum using independent lift choices, including the all-deep stratum. Distinct exponential bases and nonzero coefficients prove the recurrence order and rational series; division by |H|^r gives P_r. For a commuting additive projection W, its R-span is determinant-isotropic. The Smith exponents of that span sum to at least m, so its order is at most q^m; a coordinate line attains equality. To justify the overlap and error bounds in the frozen proof even for nonprime q, any inclusion-maximal abelian subgroup is the full preimage of its isotropic R-span (the preimage is abelian). Their sizes and intersections are therefore powers of q. Below maximum, or in a proper intersection of distinct maxima, these are at most q^(2m-1). The leading exponential coefficient consequently counts the largest-order subgroups. The 12 script cases are author-recorded finite corroboration, not rerun and not used as the universal proof.

evidence: Torres-Giese gives a general finite Dirichlet-series framework. Levit–Shwartz Theorem A gives the dominant coefficient as the number of maximum-order abelian subgroups. Their finite-field companion treats the rank-one Heisenberg case, yielding q^2 and q+1 and the commuting hierarchy at m=1. The cyclic-split Corollary 4.20 directly covers R=Z/p^m Z. Kaur–Sharma–Singh consider branching and selected low-arity probabilities over odd fields.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Finite spectrum and identification of a dominant coefficient are prior, and the field/cyclic specializations are covered even where not restated. Those evaluated cases cannot be applied verbatim to chain rings with noncyclic additive quotient and ring-valued commutator.

evidence: UT_3(R)=A ⋊ R_add, where A has a=0 in (a,b,c). For R=Z/p^m Z, the subgroup of order p^j in R_add fixes precisely the pairs with b in p^jR and unconstrained c, so |A:C_{p^j}|=p^j. Corollary 4.20 gives Dirichlet indices p^m d with d squarefree dividing p^j; summing gives coefficient sum_{j=0}^m p^j at index p^m and minus sum_{j=1}^m p^j at p^(m+1), exactly the claimed cyclic specialization. The later valuation sum for UT_3 over all R simplifies to the displayed two terms.

value.rationale: The exact higher-commutativity spectrum is a natural group invariant. Evaluating its complete two-term form over every chain ring, independent of ring characteristic or isomorphism type at fixed q,m, gives substantially more than the existence of a recurrence or a pair count. It also identifies the precise largest abelian subgroup multiplicity across the same family.
